items.title: E318 as ruled is unsound: no emitter table is editor-dead — the language server's const pass lowers every const site through the JS transformer (`transformer::ConstWorld`) over the same clone decisions, last uses and view plans, and the drop plan's per-root drop types are the §8 `drop_call_edges` the call graph and platform coloring walk (its C11 refusal is a diagnostic too)
items.body: Built and probed before shipping: with `compute_clone_sites` (and the rest of the emitter-only tail) skipped under a `Workspace::skip_emitter_tables` flag, a skipping analysis evaluated `fun build(): usize { let a = [1, 2]; mut b = a; b.push(3); a.len() } ... const build()` to 3 where the emitting one answers 2 — the const pass lowered `mut b = a` without its copy. The drop plan cannot be skipped for a second reason: `build_drop_glue` turns its per-root drop types into `drop_call_edges`, which `CallGraph::successors` and `platform_color`'s walk follow (a `@process` drop colors its owner), and `reject_conditional_temporaries` reports from it. What the tail costs on a served kolt keystroke (load 4, base): LastUse 9.2, shared reads 4.8, view/clone/hmr plans 4.3, resource types 2.2, clone sites < 1, held rows 1.1 — ~21 ms, the drop plan 5.0 beside. Doors: (a) close E318 as ruled-unsound; (b) a CONST-REACH lane — the bodies the const sites can lower, computed before the tail (a call-graph walk from the const sites, trait dispatch conservatively whole), the emitter tables computed for that lane only on a seeded analysis (a paper: an under-approximation is a silent wrong const value); (c) skip only when the program holds no const site (kolt holds 168: nothing). Rec: (a) now, (b) as a paper only if the ~21 ms is wanted after M151/M137.

items.title: E145's import-alias spans and the type-reference hover labels are rendered over every file of the world on every analysis — ~11–13 ms of a served kolt keystroke (the largest single row of the extraction tail after M148)
items.body: `collect_import_alias_spans` walks every expression and every type reference of the program with a `spelling_at` and an alias lookup each, and the `type_references` map renders a `pretty_print_type` label for every written type reference in every file (std's and lucide's included). Both are per-file and a pure function of the settled types and the text, the M148 shape: span-keyed rows per module/item (the label by `(source, span)`), skipped for a restored region, a served item's re-based with its text. The labels are read by hover only; find-references reads the (source, span, definition) triple, which stays. Measured (probe marks, load 10): 'type references labels' 11.4–15.1 ms per served keystroke.

items.title: R11's whole-program sets (`LexicalCandidates` over every binding, place and `is` test of the world) cost 7.5–14 ms of a served kolt keystroke whenever one instantiation is seeded; M149's fold now supplies the loaned captures and crossings, the three span indexes remain
items.body: An instantiation slices the candidates inside its callee's declaration, and the callee may be any module's — so the index must cover the world, but its rows are per-region facts (the binding, place and test ids with their spans): the same row family shape as M149's, indexed by span at the fold. Sizing M.

items.title: `plan_resource_drops` still re-plans every enrolled body on a served keystroke (5–9 ms on kolt): `resource_reaching_roots` sweeps every function and closure with a per-body predicate (not a live walk), and the per-root scan runs for served bodies too
items.body: The outputs a served body contributes to diagnostics are Id-only: its `drop_call_edges` (drop method, construction site) and its C11 refusals; the TypeIds (dropped bindings' types, overwrite types) are emitter inputs. A per-root record of the edges and refusals, gated by a digest of the Drop-implementing nominal set (the validator M149 asked for, needed here because these would be served verdicts), would let a seeded analysis plan live roots only — but the emitter (and the const pass, E?1) still needs `dropped_bindings` and the glue for every body it lowers, so the slice is only sound once E?1 says which bodies those are. Rec: after E?1.
